Exercise 1: Exploratory Data Analysis

#your code here

college_recent_grads %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = median)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2500, fill = "pink") +
  labs(title = "Histogram of Median",
       x = "Median",
       y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()

college_recent_grads %>% 
  select(major_category, median) %>%
  arrange(desc(median))
## # A tibble: 173 × 2
##    major_category    median
##    <chr>              <dbl>
##  1 Engineering       110000
##  2 Engineering        75000
##  3 Engineering        73000
##  4 Engineering        70000
##  5 Engineering        65000
##  6 Engineering        65000
##  7 Business           62000
##  8 Physical Sciences  62000
##  9 Engineering        60000
## 10 Engineering        60000
## # ℹ 163 more rows

Your explanation

The distribution has a positive skew. The Major category with teh highest median earnings is engineering.

Exercise 2: Exploring relationship

#your code here

college_recent_grads %>%
  filter(na.rm = TRUE) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = sharewomen, y = median)) +
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Do majors with a higher share of women have lower median earnings?",
    x = "Share of Women",
    y = "Median Earnings"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
## Warning: Removed 1 row containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_smooth()`).
## Warning: Removed 1 row containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

Your explanation

  1. the response variable is median earnings, the explanatory variable is share of women

  2. There is a weak linear correlation between medain earnings and share of women. The higher the share of women in a major, the lower the median earnings.

Exercise 3: Fit and interpret a numerical predictor

#your code here

share_fit <- lm(median ~ sharewomen, data = college_recent_grads)
summary(share_fit)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = median ~ sharewomen, data = college_recent_grads)
## 
## Residuals:
##    Min     1Q Median     3Q    Max 
## -17261  -5474  -1007   3502  57604 
## 
## Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)    56093       1705   32.90   <2e-16 ***
## sharewomen    -30670       2987  -10.27   <2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 9031 on 170 degrees of freedom
##   (1 observation deleted due to missingness)
## Multiple R-squared:  0.3828, Adjusted R-squared:  0.3791 
## F-statistic: 105.4 on 1 and 170 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16
augmented_data <- augment(share_fit) 
ggplot(augmented_data, aes(x = .fitted, y = .resid)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Residual Plot",
    x = "Predicted Values",
    y = "Residuals"
  ) + 
  theme_minimal()

Your explanation

fitted model equation: predicted median = 56093 - 30670 x sharewomen

there is no clear pattern between residuals and predicted values but they are fairly randomly scattered around the 0 line

Exercise 4: Consider a categorical variable instead

#your code here

college_recent_grads <- college_recent_grads %>%
  mutate(Engineering =
           case_when(
             major_category == "Engineering" ~ "Engineering",
             TRUE ~ "Other"
           ))

Engineering_fit <- lm(median ~ Engineering, data = college_recent_grads)
summary(Engineering_fit)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = median ~ Engineering, data = college_recent_grads)
## 
## Residuals:
##    Min     1Q Median     3Q    Max 
## -17383  -4681  -1681   3319  52617 
## 
## Coefficients:
##                  Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)         57383       1574   36.46   <2e-16 ***
## EngineeringOther   -20702       1725  -12.00   <2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 8476 on 171 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.4571, Adjusted R-squared:  0.454 
## F-statistic:   144 on 1 and 171 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16

Your explanation

  1. the baseline is engineering. the model predicting median from egineering is:

predicted median = 57383 - 20702x Engineering
